title.narrative: Validating the cultivation of crickets and the production of cricket Protein Powder the most sustainable and affordable protein in Loc Ninh, Vietnam

description.narrative: According to FAO, Food security and climate change are becoming a huge issue. By 2050 the world population will reach 9.5 billion people and food production needs to expand 70% to keep up with this growth which will be hard under the current production system. More efficient and sustainable food sources are required to feed the world and crickets may provide the solution to this as its by-products are rich in protein and believed to be better, cheaper and more sustainable than other protein sources, such as livestock and salmon. Cricket One B.V. has developed intensive farming technologies and processes crickets into protein, oil and other high value-added products for the US and EU food and supplement industry for which it established a processing facility in Vietnam. Increased production will have a positive impact on the environment using sustainable production methods and replacing traditional (animal) protein sources as it uses cassava waste to feed and breed the crickets through micro breeding units planted out at cassava farms. This in turn allows for circular farming and additional income streams for smallholder farmers involved, improving their agricultural practices and more importantly, their livelihoods. To prepare for future investments, Technical Assistance (DGGF-TA) provided support to upscale the activities and increase production and export capacity of premium cricket protein powder. The project included preparing for international certification with HPPC and obtaining Novel Food Certification, to develop and install breeding stations at different farmers’ sites and to further develop cricket protein isolation for product diversification. The project supported 8 female direct jobs, 10 indirect jobs and enabled knowledge transfer by training 35 people, of which 25 local cassava farmers on producing cricket feed, breeding high quality crickets and circular farming using their cassava waste which enables them to earn up to 5 times higher incomes. Since the project CricketOne has put 3 central farms into operation to secure 40% its raw materials demand and set-up a central processing factory and Cricket One is now becoming one of the largest global suppliers of cricket protein.
